6
In which example is it not possible for the underlined object to be in equilibrium?
A
An aeroplane climbs at a steady rate.
B
An aeroplane tows a glider at a constant altitude.
C
A speedboat changes direction at a constant speed.
D
Two boats tow a ship into harbour.

hints: Look at the motion of each underlined object, especially whether its speed and its direction of travel both stay the same.
Recall that equilibrium needs zero resultant force, so by $F = ma$ the acceleration must be zero and velocity must be constant as a vector.
Check which example keeps speed constant but changes direction, and ask why that still means the velocity is changing.
walkthrough: Equilibrium for a point object means the vector sum of forces is zero, so from $F = ma$ the acceleration $a$ must be zero.
Zero acceleration means constant velocity, which requires both constant speed and constant direction of motion.
An aeroplane climbing at a steady rate, a glider towed at constant altitude, and a ship towed into harbour can all move in a straight line with constant velocity, so balanced forces are possible.
A speedboat changing direction at constant speed has changing velocity because velocity is a vector and direction is part of it.
Changing velocity means non-zero acceleration, so a resultant centripetal force must act and forces cannot balance. This is option C.

A.explanation: The aeroplane has constant velocity in a straight line, so acceleration is zero and the forces can balance.

B.explanation: The glider can move with constant velocity at constant altitude, so thrust, drag, lift and weight can have zero resultant.

C.explanation: Changing direction means the velocity vector changes, so there is acceleration and a non-zero resultant force is required.

D.explanation: The ship can be towed slowly with constant velocity, so the two tow forces plus drag can balance to zero resultant.
